s1.syndrome_frame: Systemic inflammatory syndrome with fever, fatigue, and abdominal tenderness, progressing over several days
salient_findings: Daily fevers exceeding 39°C
Tenderness in the left lower quadrant
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT)
Pancytopenia (leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia)
Nonspecific inflammatory changes on CT imaging
Dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate on peritoneal biopsy
key_facts: Four days of fevers, fatigue, nausea, headaches, and malaise
Blood pressure of 82/50 mm Hg (responded to fluids)
Nonspecific inflammatory fat stranding and peritoneal thickening on CT
Peritoneal biopsy showed dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD8, CD7, CD43, CD5 (partial loss), TIA-1, granzyme B, CD2, and TCRβ F1

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated ferritin, fever, and cytopenias are consistent with HLH, and bone marrow biopsy suggested HLH

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Peritoneal biopsy showed dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate, and immunohistochemistry results are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms, abnormal liver function tests, and atypical lymphoid infiltrate on biopsy are consistent with T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammatory syndrome with fever, fatigue, and abdominal tenderness could be consistent with SLE, although other findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Adult-onset Still's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammatory syndrome with fever, fatigue, and abdominal tenderness could be consistent with AOSD, although other findings are not typical

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with prolonged fevers, elevated ferritin levels, and evidence of hemophagocytosis on bone marrow biopsy, along with elevated interleukin (IL)-2R alpha levels, are key indicators of Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). The patient's laboratory results, including significantly elevated liver enzymes (AST and ALT), low leukocyte count, and thrombocytopenia, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While the peritoneal biopsy showed a dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate, which could suggest a lymphoma, the overall clinical and laboratory picture, including the systemic nature of the illness and the specific findings like very high ferritin levels and hemophagocytosis, points more towards HLH.

rejected.label: T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Similar to subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, the presence of a T-cell lymphoid infiltrate could suggest T-cell lymphoma, but the systemic symptoms and specific laboratory findings like high ferritin and evidence of hemophagocytosis are more characteristic of HLH.

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Although SLE can present with systemic symptoms and elevated inflammatory markers, the specific combination of very high ferritin levels, hemophagocytosis on bone marrow biopsy, and the absence of other classic SLE criteria (like a positive ANA) make HLH a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Adult-onset Still's disease
rejected.why: Adult-onset Still's disease can present with fever, rash, and elevated inflammatory markers, but the presence of hemophagocytosis and the very high levels of ferritin, along with the specific immunohistochemical findings, are more indicative of HLH.
